question: If the Mode is 3 and it is given that the Mode is (3)/(2) times the Mean, find the square of the product of the Median and the Mean.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mode = 3 and Mode = (3/2) × Mean ⇒ Mean = 2

Use relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

3 = 3 Median − 4 ⇒ Median = 7/3

Product = Mean × Median = 2 × (7/3) = 14/3

**∴ Square = 196/9 = 21(7)/(9) **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode = 3 and Mode = (3/2) × Mean

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ 3 = (3/2) × Mean

⇒ Mean = 2

⇒ Substitute in formula: 3 = 3 Median − 2 × 2

⇒ 3 = 3 Median − 4

⇒ 3 Median = 7

⇒ Median = 7/3

⇒ Product = Mean × Median = 2 × (7/3) = 14/3

⇒ Square = (14/3)² = 196/9 = 21(7)/(9) 

**∴ The correct answer is 21(7)/(9) .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean (used for moderately skewed data)

Mean from Mode

If Mode = k × Mean, then Mean = Mode ÷ k

Square of Product

(ab)² = a²b²
